key_insight: A physics-informed neural network can learn how whole-system impedance poles and residues change with operating conditions, enabling fast small-signal stability assessment across the full power-flow space in multi-inverter grids.
engineering_relevance: This provides grid operators with a practical tool to anticipate oscillation risks, locate their causes, and support safer generation dispatch in inverter-dominated power systems.
method: Train a PINN on step-response data from a limited set of EMT simulations.
Use the learned model to predict poles and residues of the whole-system impedance/admittance transfer functions.
Map how stability and oscillatory modes evolve as power flow varies across operating points.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on both a 2-IBR system and a 4-IBR system using EMT-simulation-derived step-response data.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness and quality of the EMT training cases, so extrapolation beyond the sampled operating space may be risky.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Small-Signal Stability in Multi-Inverter Power Systems
